title: DoorInteraction.cs
summary: A standalone interactable door: drop it on a door mesh. E fades the screen out, moves the player to the other side of the doorway facing away from it, and fades back in. The door never swings, so its collider keeps the doorway shut. Handles range detection, an emissive highlight and a shared UI Toolkit key prompt.

notes.match: public float interactRange = 2.4f;      // from the middle of the door, flat on the floor
notes.text: How close (flat on the floor, from the middle of the door) the player must be to use it.
Color and strength of the emissive glow shown while this is the door the player can use.

notes.match: static readonly List<DoorInteraction> Active = new List<DoorInteraction>();
notes.text: Every enabled door registers here, so two doors in reach at once (a hallway) can agree that only the nearer one answers.

notes.match: static UIE.VisualElement _prompt;   // the shared bottom-centre key prompt (InteractPrompt.uxml), one for all doors
notes.text: One prompt element for all doors, built from the shared InteractPrompt.uxml (a UI Toolkit screen), not an OnGUI label.
Cached PropertyToID is faster than passing the string "_EmissionColor" every time the highlight changes.
Locates the player once at Start; doors don't need to track it afterwards.
Only touches the highlight and the prompt when the in-range state actually changes.
Same OR-with-mobile pattern as the collectibles and NPC conversations: the on-screen E button sets MobileInput.InteractPressed.
Not while a conversation, menu or story shot has the player held.
Two doors can be in reach at once; only the closer one answers.
Shows "[ E ]  Use Door" while any door is in reach. The prompt sits a row above the NPC talk prompt (.doors in InteractPrompt.uss), so both can show at once.
